Scales decide how a data column becomes a visual property; getting them right is most of what makes a chart readable.
Use a colour-vision-deficiency-safe palette such as [Okabe-Ito](../reference/scales/scale-okabe-ito.qmd) for categories, a perceptually uniform ramp such as [Viridis](../reference/scales/scale-viridis-c.qmd) for continuous values, and a diverging gradient only when the data has a meaningful midpoint.
Beyond colour, these examples map size, shape, opacity, stroke, and line style, and show manual and binned variants of each family.
See the [accessibility guide](../guides/accessibility.qmd) for the reasoning behind these defaults.
Every example ships its full source: click **View source** to copy it.
